title: Extracting Cultural Commonsense Knowledge at Scale
measurement_description: The paper measures the quality of extracted cultural commonsense knowledge (CCSK) assertions regarding different religious groups, specifically evaluating them on plausibility (general truthfulness), commonality (how mainstream the knowledge is), distinctiveness (discriminative informativeness), and offensiveness. It also measures the ability of GPT-3 to generate accurate socio-cultural religious knowledge and use it in downstream question-answering tasks.
findings: The paper found that extracted assertions about religious groups and occupations were significantly more distinctive than assertions about geographical regions. In the religion domain, the generated assertions achieved a high average plausibility score of 1.51 (out of 2.0), a commonality score of 1.29, and a distinctiveness score of 1.22. The system successfully filtered out most offensive generalizations, resulting in only 1% of assertions being marked as offensive. Furthermore, it demonstrated that GPT-3 often generates overly generic responses regarding cultural/religious topics, and providing the model with explicitly extracted religious commonsense knowledge significantly improves its performance in QA tasks.
